About

Every number should trace back to its source.

Business intelligence taught me to ask first whether the business can trust the number.

I am a Data Analyst and BI Developer with 5+ years of experience in SQL, PostgreSQL, MS SQL Server and Power BI, building reporting and dashboards across mortgage lending, banking, oil and gas, and medical devices. Most of that work is about data quality and reporting accuracy: modeling the data properly, documenting the architecture, and explaining the result to people who will never write a DAX measure.

The same habit runs through my data science work: Python with pandas and scikit-learn for classification, forecasting and segmentation, evaluated on held-out data and explained in terms a stakeholder can act on, then published back into Power BI where decisions get made.

I am now applying that habit to AI as well. I evaluate LLM responses for incorrect reasoning and factual consistency, write and test prompts, label data against clear guidelines, and design human-in-the-loop workflows. Alongside that, I build practical agent projects in Python with LLM APIs: retrieval over documents, SQL-based assistants and automation pipelines.

I am interested in AI training projects involving response evaluation, prompt creation, structured reasoning, domain-specific annotation and quality assurance for AI systems.

What I do

  • Dashboards & reportingPower BI and SQL reporting that teams rely on daily: modeled, documented and refreshed on schedule.
  • Analysis & predictive modelingStatistics and machine learning in Python: classification, forecasting and segmentation, explained for the people who decide.
  • AI evaluation & annotationRubrics, labeling guidelines and QA passes that make model judgments consistent and auditable.
  • AI agent prototypesRAG assistants, SQL agents and document automation with human review, built on LLM APIs.

Data SciencePortfolio build

Loan default risk model

Context

Lenders need to flag risky loans early without turning away good borrowers. The exercise: rank default risk in a way an underwriter can question.

Approach

Feature engineering on synthetic loan data (debt-to-income, credit score, loan-to-value, delinquency history), gradient boosting with class weights, 5-fold cross-validation, threshold tuning for recall, and SHAP values for per-loan explanations.

Outcome

ROC-AUC of 0.87 on the holdout set against a 0.79 logistic baseline, calibrated probabilities, and a plain-language reason attached to every flagged loan.

Document Q&A with RAG

Context

Policy and procedure documents are long, and people want direct answers they can verify against the page.

Approach

Chunked and embedded a document set, retrieved the top passages for each question, and prompted the model to answer only from retrieved text with inline citations. Every answer is logged with its sources for review.

Outcome

Answers carry page-level citations, and the assistant says plainly when the documents do not cover a question, which is exactly the behavior an evaluator looks for.

Data SciencePortfolio build

Device demand forecasting

Context

Devices with a shelf life make inventory a timing problem: order too early and stock expires, too late and you miss demand.

Approach

Modeled monthly demand with seasonal components, compared statsmodels and Prophet, back-tested with rolling-origin cross-validation, and reported an 80% prediction interval instead of a single number.

Outcome

6.4% MAPE over an 8-month horizon against 11.8% for a seasonal naive baseline, with the forecast translated into a reorder signal and an expiry-risk estimate.

AI & LLMPortfolio build

LLM response evaluation dashboard

Context

AI training teams need judgments about model output that stay consistent across raters and can be audited afterwards.

Approach

Wrote a five-dimension rubric (accuracy, grounding, completeness, tone, safety) with labeling guidelines, scored a batch with multiple raters, measured agreement with Cohen's kappa, and compared two prompt versions with a win rate and confidence interval.

Outcome

A disagreement queue that shows where the guidelines are unclear, and a score distribution that shows which dimensions a prompt change actually moved.

Data SciencePortfolio build

Banking customer segmentation

Context

A bank's customers behave very differently, and a single average hides that. The exercise: find stable groups a marketing team can act on.

Approach

Engineered twelve behavioral features from synthetic transaction data, scaled them, chose k with silhouette scores, and reduced to two principal components to inspect the clusters. Wrote a one-line profile for each segment.

Outcome

Four interpretable segments with sizes and traits, published to a Power BI page so teams can size campaigns and watch movement between segments each quarter.

Data quality monitor for reporting pipelines

Context

BI reports rarely crash when upstream data goes wrong. They quietly show the wrong number.

Approach

Wrote Python checks for freshness, row counts, null rates, schema drift and referential integrity, added a seasonal baseline with a ±3σ band for row counts, and surfaced results on a status page.

Outcome

A partial load that cut a fact table by 34% is flagged the same night instead of appearing as an unexplained dip in a monthly report.

AI & LLMPortfolio build

Document automation with a review gate

Context

Operations teams receive a steady stream of documents that need sorting and data entry, and fully automatic handling is not acceptable when confidence is low.

Approach

Built an agent pipeline that classifies each document, extracts fields into a schema, routes anything under a confidence threshold to a review queue, and writes approved records to PostgreSQL. Reviewer corrections flow back as labels.

Outcome

Most documents pass straight through, the rest reach a person with the model's draft already filled in, and every correction improves the next run.

-- A typical time-intelligence measure behind a yearly / quarterly view
Funded Volume YoY % =
VAR CurrentPeriod = [Funded Volume]
VAR PriorPeriod =
    CALCULATE ( [Funded Volume], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( CurrentPeriod - PriorPeriod, PriorPeriod )

Measures, not magic

Patterns like this sit behind the yearly, quarterly, monthly and daily reports I build. The same instinct carries into AI evaluation: define the comparison clearly, handle the edge cases, and make the result reproducible.
